records.name: Aksels
records.facts_used: The Nordic-name manual gives the exact Norwegian correspondence Aksel → Aksels. This documents one route by which the name is rendered in Latvian. It does not require selecting the catalogue’s doubtful alternative etymologies as a universal explanation. The exact row appears in the 2003 manual on printed page 214. This dates the published rendering recommendation. It does not identify the first Latvian birth registration, and earlier dates for other spellings are not transferred to this form.
records.reason: Exact-form evidence supports a reviewed history in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Accepted narrative documents the Norwegian rendering and qualified competing catalogue explanations; possible 1891/1817 are not secure first dates. Checked location: Nordic manual PDF 110 / printed 214: Aksel → Aksels; catalogue p. 47. Original PDF pages were visually read where used; catalogue transcriptions remain attributed.

records.name: Algis
records.facts_used: The dictionary explicitly identifies Algis as a short form of Algimantas and Algirdas. Salys’s calendar also lists Algis independently. The exact form is documented in the Senn–Salys Lithuanian–German dictionary of 1968, reprinted in Salys’s collected writings in 1983. This is a dated linguistic record of the name and its relationships; it does not identify the first child registered with this spelling.

records.name: Gabija
records.facts_used: Gabija is a name from Lithuanian mythology, associated with the goddess of fire and the home. Maciejauskienė includes it among newer names in Salys’s calendar. The mythological name and its modern given-name use belong to different historical contexts. The historical calendar for 1964 prints Gabija (Gabė) on 9 January. This is direct evidence of the name’s twentieth-century calendar use and of the short form Gabė. It is not a date for the beginning of the older mythological tradition.
records.reason: Exact-form evidence supports a reviewed history in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Do not state the proposed gaubti root as verified; history uses the documented mythological name and twentieth-century calendar adoption. Checked location: 1964 calendar PDF 301 / printed 286; Maciejauskienė PDF 2; curated Gabija mythology paragraph. Original PDF pages were visually read where used; catalogue transcriptions remain attributed.

records.name: Veli
records.facts_used: Rajandi places Veli in the Estonian “brother-name” group with Vello. In this group he connects Finnish Veikko with veli, “brother”. That is a documented family association, not a personality trait assigned to the bearer. In a sample of 4,000 adult men changing names in 1935–1940, Rajandi counts three choices of Veli. The figure concerns that historical sample of name changes. It is not a total of births, all bearers or the present population.
records.reason: Exact-form evidence supports a reviewed history in five languages.
records.uncertainties: Checked location: Rajandi PDF 175 / printed 177, 3 of 4000 adult name changes 1935–40; Mägiste PDF 53 / printed 51. Original PDF pages were visually read where used; catalogue transcriptions remain attributed.

records.name: Velvo

These dated linguistic records show the form’s place in naming proposals; they are not an independently inspected first birth entry.

records.name: Väiko
records.facts_used: Rajandi explicitly sends Väiko to both Veigo and Vello. It therefore belongs to his brother-name discussion, but the cross-reference alone does not prove which full form stood behind any particular person’s Väiko. The form and its relationships are documented in Edgar Rajandi’s Raamat nimedest, published in Tallinn in 1966. The book records the naming traditions known at that time. Its publication date documents a linguistic treatment, rather than the name’s invention or its first birth registration.
